title: The particle identity of dark matter
bottleneck: Dark matter's gravitational effects are mapped in exquisite detail, yet after decades of direct detection, indirect detection, and collider production searches, not a single dark matter particle has been identified. Every major candidate class, WIMPs, axions, sterile neutrinos, has a shrinking but nonzero allowed region, and the true answer could lie somewhere entirely unconsidered.
why_it_blocks: Dark matter is five sixths of all matter; not knowing what it is means the dominant form of matter in the universe is a complete mystery, stalling cosmology and particle physics alike.
current_state: LZ recently reported a single unexplained 248 keV nuclear-recoil event at 2.6 sigma, intriguing but far below discovery threshold, while the main WIMP searches continue to report world-leading null results.
